title: Sequenced quarterly plan for enterprise-isolated deployments (VPC/on-prem): waves, gates, and OKR mapping
creator: Ethan Park
description:
Objective:
Define a concrete, sequenced quarterly roadmap for enterprise-isolated deployments (VPC + on-prem) that maps incremental capability deliveries to OKRs, establishes wave-based rollout gates, and clarifies cross-functional responsibilities. This ticket produces the canonical plan for Q2 2026 that will be used to coordinate Eng, Design, Security, and Solutions.
background_and_scope:
Background: Customers evaluating Private deployments repeatedly cite (1) predictable upgrade windows, (2) clear compatibility guarantees for enterprise networking, and (3) auditability of controls as blockers to adoption. Past roadmaps focused on feature breadth; this plan focuses on predictable sequencing and gating so we can safely increase install cadence while minimizing customer disruption.

Scope: The deliverable covers the quarter-level milestones for VPC onboarding improvements, on‑prem install hygiene (upgrade tooling, rollback), RBAC and audit log enhancements, and a gated compatibility matrix. Does NOT include low-level kernel/runtime changes (ENG tickets will be linked) but includes acceptance criteria and SLO thresholds for those changes to pass rollout gates.
outcomes_and_metrics:
Primary outcomes: (1) Increase Private trial-to-conversion by 15% by ensuring customers can complete a full upgrade/rollback rehearsal; (2) Reduce support incidents during rollout windows by 40%; (3) Meet security/compliance gates for SOC2 and EU data residency customers.

Success metrics (OKR-mapped):
- OKR 1.1 (Onboard): +15% conversion within 90 days of trial start attributable to documented upgrade/runbook.
- OKR 2.2 (Reliability): <2 P0/P1 incidents per quarter attributable to Private upgrade flows.
- OKR 3.3 (Compliance): Full audit trail coverage for KMS operations in all staged environments (pass internal audit checklist).
milestones: Wave 0: Internal alpha (developer-only) — 2026-04-01 to 2026-04-15: baseline sanity, upgrade/rollback rehearsal in lab clusters
Gate A: Security & Upgrade Readiness — complete design review and security sign-off for RBAC and KMS flows by 2026-04-20
Wave 1: Pilot customers (3 customers) — 2026-04-21 to 2026-05-12: first customer rehearsals with dedicated support and runbook walkthroughs
Gate B: Compatibility Matrix Validation — prove backward compatibility for 2 major orgs and 3 supported OS/Network configs by 2026-05-15
Wave 2: Controlled rollouts (10 customers) — 2026-05-16 to 2026-06-10: expand pilot, measure SLOs and incident rate
Gate C: Operations Freeze & GA Readiness — final checklist, playbooks, training, and billing integration complete by 2026-06-12
Release: GA to customer self-service — 2026-06-18: production enablement and public docs published
acceptance_criteria: Automated upgrade test runbook executes end-to-end (upgrade + rollback) in lab with zero manual steps for core path
Audit logs capture KMS operations and supervisor approvals for every upgrade in pilot clusters
Console shows token-level cost impact for Private deployments during pilot so Solutions can advise customers
At least 2 pilot customers complete a full upgrade rehearsal and sign a readiness note
No severity P0 incidents in Wave 1 and acceptable incident trend in Wave 2 (incident rate < 0.5 per customer-week)
Security review documented and signed (security_review_required = true) with open findings <= 2 low-priority items
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Kernel/runtime incompatibilities discovered late causing rollback complexity. Mitigation: isolate runtime changes into separate ENG backlog items, require a canary kernel channel and immediate fallback policy.

Risk: Customer networking variability (firewalls, restrictive NAT) causes failed installs. Mitigation: create a standardized network preflight checklist and a lightweight connectivity diagnostic tool for Solutions.

Risk: Audit/Compliance scope creep when engaging large regulated customers. Mitigation: define minimum compliance checklist for GA and create an enterprise add-on for deeper audit integrations post-GA.
Risk: Support load spikes during pilot. Mitigation: reserve dedicated on-call rotation and create runbook-led troubleshooting playbooks for first 6 pilot customers.
decisions: Decision 1: Sequence by operational risk, not feature completeness — upgrades/rollback tooling first, then RBAC & audit polish.
Decision 2: Use wave-based customer selection: internal → small pilot → controlled rollouts → GA.
Decision 3: GA will require completed Security & Ops sign-off; partial GA (early access) will be provided to select enterprise partners under NDA.
cross_team_actions: ENG: Create a public compatibility matrix doc and automated validation suite (ENG-34121)
ENG: Implement an upgrade canary channel and rollback scripts (ENG-35567)
SEC: Complete KMS integration review and produce audit checklist
DX: Draft pilot onboarding templates and runbooks for Solutions
GTM: Prepare pilot contract addendum and pricing guardrails
